request.prompt:
You are the Stage 4 Synthesist. Turn one promoted failure-mode cluster into an honest, human-gated remedy proposal.

Most frustrations do not deserve a skill. Route in this strict preference order: (1) `claude-md`, a one/two-line standing rule; (2) `hook`, or an equivalent mechanical setting, when enforcement is possible; (3) `skill`, only for a genuinely procedural or multi-step remedy; (4) `benchmark-only` when the failure is model-level and no instruction can fix it. Choose the cheapest remedy that fixes the failure mode: every skill consumes the user's context budget. `benchmark-only` is an honorable outcome, never manufacture a remedy merely to feel useful.

If the only sensible remedy target is Codex-side (`AGENTS.md` or `~/.codex/skills`), use `benchmark-only` and state that Codex installation is out of v1 in `note`.

You must check every existing-remedy digest below. State a `dedup` item for each one with `clear` or `overlap`. Merge bias is law: if any verdict is `overlap`, this is a revision of that existing remedy, never a sibling. Set `overlap_action.revises` to the exact existing reference.

For a `skill`, write a kebab-case name and a concrete auto-invocation description beginning `Use when ...`; this description is the trigger. The body must be substantive Markdown. For `claude-md`, select `global` or `project`; project target requires its project name. For `hook`, give a Claude Code event and a command sketch. For `benchmark-only`, explain the measurement-only outcome in `note`.

The upstream classifier deliberately over-merges. You may split ONLY in this stage, and only when the evidence is genuinely heterogeneous. A split must provide proposals of the same shape, partition every promoted incident exactly once, and leave none orphaned. Otherwise return one proposal covering the group.

TAXONOMY GIST:
destructive-action: deleted/overwrote/reset without care

PROMOTED EVIDENCE:
BEGIN PROMOTED EVIDENCE incident_id=2 project=aurora
One-liner: Deleted a file without obtaining user permission first
Preceding request:
The constraint from the opening note was discarded again.

Agent activity digest:
Assistant: Synthetic acknowledgement.

Frustrated message:
What are you doing? You deleted the fake migration without asking.

Following exchange:

END PROMOTED EVIDENCE

EXISTING SKILLS (name and description only):
- skill:$HOME/.claude/skills/fake-verify-before-claim/SKILL.md | name=fake-verify-before-claim | description=Use when a completion claim requires verification.

S2S-MANAGED CLAUDE.MD BLOCKS:
- claude-md:$HOME/.claude/CLAUDE.md#1 | # Fake Release Discipline

Before reporting a fake release as complete, run its declared verification
command and report the result plainly.

PENDING OR INSTALLED S2S PROPOSALS:
- (none)


Your prior draft failed local validation. Correct the SKILL.md/frontmatter, dedup, and evidence partition exactly.

structured_output.failure_statement: Agent deletes or destructively overwrites a file via a shell command without first asking the user for permission, including overriding an explicit prior standing instruction not to touch that file.

remedy_content.command_sketch: Shell script/regex gate invoked on every Bash tool call before execution. Inspects tool_input.command against a destructive-pattern list (rm, rm -rf, git reset --hard, git clean -f/-fd, git checkout -- ., git push --force*, DROP TABLE, TRUNCATE, unlink, rmdir, shred, > on an existing tracked file). If matched, the hook returns a deny/ask decision with a message like 'Destructive command detected: <cmd>. Confirm with the user before running this — do not proceed on an assumed or prior-turn approval unless it named this exact action.' The hook does not fire on read-only or additive commands (mkdir, cp, mv into a new path, git add/commit).
remedy_content.notes: Scope to Bash first since that is where the observed incident occurred; equivalent file-clearing via Edit/Write (writing an empty/truncated file over an existing one) is a plausible follow-on case worth covering later but is out of scope for this v1 hook to keep the pattern list precise and avoid false positives on legitimate small edits.

structured_output.routing_rationale: The agent deleted a file without asking, in direct violation of an explicit standing instruction the user had already given ("the constraint from the opening note was discarded again"). This is a destructive-action failure where instruction-following already failed once — the base system prompt for this environment already contains a detailed "Executing actions with care" policy requiring confirmation before deletes, and it was still ignored. Adding another claude-md line would be the cheapest fix in the abstract, but it is not credible here because a near-equivalent instruction already existed and was overridden; the failure is precisely that a verbal instruction was not load-bearing enough. That pushes this to the next rung: a mechanical PreToolUse hook that intercepts destructive Bash commands (rm, git reset --hard, git clean -f, force-push, DROP/TRUNCATE, etc.) and blocks execution pending explicit confirmation, rather than trusting the model to remember and apply the rule unprompted. This is not a multi-step procedure, so a skill would be overkill and would burn context budget for no benefit over a hook. It is also not a model-level limitation requiring benchmark-only — the fix is enforceable mechanically.
